questions.question: What is a code of ethics?
options: A list of penalties for employees caught stealing
A formal statement of the values and standards of behaviour a business commits itself to
The set of double-entry rules every bookkeeper must follow
A contract between the business and the revenue service

questions.question: Whom does a business's code of ethics bind?
options: Only the accountants and bookkeepers who handle the records
Only the owner, since the business belongs to the owner
All parties in the financial environment — owners, managers, bookkeepers, employees, and dealings with customers, suppliers and the state
Only employees who signed it when they were appointed

questions.question: Why is trust called the precondition for the whole discipline of Accounting?
options: Because auditors are legally required to trust the figures they check
Because financial information only has value if its readers can rely on the figures being honestly made
Because trusted businesses pay less tax on their profits
Because trust removes the need for internal control systems

subtopics.title: The Seven Characteristics, Defined for Marks

questions.question: An owner banks each day's takings in full, obeying every rule she sets for her own staff. Which characteristic is this?
options: Leadership
Materiality
Sustainability
Fairness

questions.question: Which characteristic is defined as consistently sticking to rules, procedures and standards, even under pressure?
options: Transparency
Accountability
Discipline
Responsible management

questions.question: A manager reports a loss to the owner and accepts the consequences instead of hiding it. Which characteristic is shown?
options: Sustainability
Accountability
Leadership
Discipline

questions.question: How do transparency and accountability overlap?
options: They are two names for the same characteristic
Transparency applies to owners while accountability applies only to employees
Openness of records and decisions is what makes it possible to answer for them — transparency enables accountability
Accountability replaces transparency once a business appoints an accountant

subtopics.title: Ethics Under Pressure — the Scenarios That Matter

questions.question: The owner of Mokoena Hardware orders his bookkeeper to leave Saturday cash sales out of the records to reduce tax. Which pair of characteristics does the OWNER breach most directly?
options: Sustainability and materiality
Leadership and fairness
Discipline and going concern
Transparency and prudence

questions.question: A cellphone-repair shop fits second-hand parts while advertising and charging for new ones. Why does TRANSPARENCY fail here?
options: Because the shop's prices are higher than its competitors' prices
Because the customer cannot see what was actually done to the phone
Because second-hand parts are illegal to use in repairs
Because the shop did not record the sale in its journals

questions.question: A car wash pipes chemical runoff into the storm drain feeding the community stream to avoid disposal costs. Which characteristic is breached most directly?
options: Sustainability
Discipline
Accountability
Fairness

subtopics.title: The Exam Method for Ethics Questions

questions.question: What is the correct order of the four-move method for an ethics question?
options: Name the characteristic, state the consequence, identify the issue, argue the link
State the issue in plain words, name the characteristic, argue the link, give consequence and correction
Give the correction, name the characteristic, state the issue, argue the link
Argue the link, state the issue, give the consequence, name the characteristic

questions.question: Why does an answer like 'this behaviour is dishonest and very wrong' earn no marks on its own?
options: Because ethics questions must always be answered with calculations
Because it moralises without naming a characteristic or using its definition in the argument
Because dishonesty is a legal issue, not an ethical one
Because the word 'wrong' may never appear in an answer

questions.question: A learner answers only: 'Transparency, accountability, fairness.' What is the flaw?
options: The characteristics are named in the wrong order
Naming without applying — no characteristic is tied to a specific fact of the scenario
Three characteristics can never apply to one scenario
The learner left out the definition of a code of ethics

questions.question: The captain is at practice on time, every time, whether she feels like it or not. Which characteristic is that?
options: Discipline
Fairness
Transparency
Sustainability

questions.question: After a heavy defeat, the captain stands up first and owns her share of the blame. Which characteristic is shown?
options: Leadership
Responsible management
Accountability
Discipline

questions.question: The captain refuses to win by hurting opponents or bending rules, because the team's name must survive into next season. Which characteristic does this show?
options: Materiality
Sustainability
Transparency
Accountability

questions.question: A customer is charged twice for one loaf; the manager pulls the till record, confirms the error and refunds it. Which characteristic made the honesty PROVABLE?
options: Transparency — a till record existed and could be checked
Sustainability — the shop plans to trade for many years
Leadership — the manager is senior to the cashier
Discipline — the cashier works quickly at the till

questions.question: An electrician offers a cheaper 'cash, no paperwork' price. Which characteristic is traded away FIRST by designing the deal to leave no trace?
options: Sustainability
Fairness
Transparency
Discipline

questions.question: A tuck-shop owner is offered half-price cool drinks from 'the back of a warehouse, no questions asked'. Why do sustainability and responsible management both answer no?
options: Because cool drinks spoil too quickly to be resold at a profit
Because one bargain today is being traded against the shop's name and community trust tomorrow
Because the shop's fridge is too small for extra stock
Because half-price stock must always be recorded as drawings

subtopics.title: Why Good Ethics Is Good Business

questions.question: The salon charges exactly the price on the board, every client, every visit. Which characteristic converts into which business advantage?
options: Fairness converts into loyal, returning clients
Sustainability converts into lower rent
Discipline converts into cheaper stock
Accountability converts into faster haircuts

questions.question: Why do honest, complete records help the salon get a bank loan for a second chair?
options: Because banks are legally forced to lend to any business with records
Because transparency lets the bank see precisely what the salon earns, making the figures credible
Because keeping records reduces the interest rate on all loans automatically
Because the records prove the salon has never made a loss

questions.question: What is the two-sided argument for the importance of a code of ethics?
options: Ethics reduces tax and increases prices
Ethics protects the business from the costs of dishonesty AND earns it the profits of being trusted
Ethics replaces internal control and saves the cost of audits
Ethics guarantees profit in the short term and long term
